steps.title: New: five more benchmarks, each labeled by source
steps.narration: The dashboard's main chart now tracks five more market benchmarks -- including the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, and Dow indexes -- right alongside the originals.
steps.point_out: Look at the legend under the chart: the five new lines each carry a small tag like (Stooq), (Yahoo), or (FRED-macro proxy) showing exactly where that data comes from, and every line now has its own distinct color.

steps.title: Every regime label links to its evidence
steps.narration: Clicking the market regime's evidence link takes you straight to the page that keeps every claim honest.
steps.point_out: The Evidence page still shows every trading idea's real, unfiltered test result -- nothing is marked proven without passing a strict, independent check.

target.name: See evidence proven in this regime →

steps.title: New: see exactly where the index data comes from
steps.narration: The Data Manager page now has a table that spells out, for every benchmark and index line, who supplied the data and how far back it honestly goes.
steps.point_out: The new provenance table lists all ten series with a vendor badge and a real first-recorded date -- several tracing all the way back to 1996.

steps.title: The stock leaderboard stays clean
steps.narration: Even with the new benchmark data loaded in, the main stock leaderboard keeps listing only real, tradable companies.
steps.point_out: None of the new index or macro symbols show up in this list, and the total company count still lines up with the Data Manager page.

steps.title: Open a company's price history
steps.narration: Every company on the leaderboard has its own detail page with a full price chart.
steps.point_out: The candlestick chart with its moving averages loads cleanly, with a simple toggle nearby to widen the view.

steps.title: Zoom out to thirty years of history in one click
steps.narration: One click swaps the recent few years for the company's entire multi-decade price history.
steps.point_out: The chart widens dramatically, and the caption honestly notes the older stretch is weekly-sampled to keep things fast.
